questions.question: Pacinian corpuscles in joint capsules respond to:

options.A: High-frequency vibration and rapid changes in pressure
options.C: Slow sustained stretch of the capsule

questions.explanation: Type II (Pacinian) receptors are rapidly adapting mechanoreceptors that detect vibration and acceleration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Free nerve endings (type IV receptors) in joint structures are sensitive to:
questions.explanation: Type IV receptors are nociceptors in the capsule, ligaments and fat pads.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Golgi tendon-organ-like endings in ligaments (type III receptors) are sensitive to:

options.A: Stretch or tension in the ligaments

questions.explanation: Type III endings monitor extreme ranges of ligament tension.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Ruffini endings in joint capsules respond to:
questions.explanation: Type I (Ruffini) endings are slowly adapting receptors signalling joint position and capsular stretch.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sympathetic stimulation causes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Sympathetic activity relaxes the detrusor and closes the sphincter; bladder contraction is parasympathetic.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Parasympathetic activation causes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The parasympathetic system constricts the pupil (miosis).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Axons conduct impulses ______ the cell body.
questions.explanation: Dendrites receive signals towards the soma; the axon carries them away.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A fibres are:
questions.explanation: Group A fibres have the highest conduction velocity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: C fibres are:
questions.explanation: C fibres carry slow pain and postganglionic sympathetic impulses.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A-delta fibres carry:
questions.explanation: A-delta fibres conduct fast (sharp) pain and cold.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A-alpha fibres carry:
questions.explanation: A-alpha are the largest fibres (Ia afferents and alpha motor neurons).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A-gamma fibres supply the:
questions.explanation: Gamma motor neurons set the sensitivity of the muscle spindle.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: B fibres are:
questions.explanation: B fibres are myelinated autonomic preganglionic fibres.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The total volume of CSF in an adult is about:
questions.explanation: Adults have about 150 mL of CSF, renewed several times a day.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Normal CSF pressure in an adult (lateral decubitus) is about:
questions.explanation: Normal lumbar opening pressure is about 70-180 mm H2O.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal protein content of CSF in an adult is:
questions.explanation: CSF protein is normally 15-45 mg/dL; it rises in meningitis and GBS.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: After systole, the volume of blood remaining in the ventricle (end-systolic volume) is about:
questions.explanation: End-diastolic volume is about 120-130 mL; stroke volume about 70 mL; end-systolic volume about 50-60 mL.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal value of stroke volume is about:
questions.explanation: Normal resting stroke volume is 60-100 mL.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) is about:
questions.explanation: Normal LVEDP is 5-12 mm Hg; it rises in left heart failure.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Myocardial oxygen demand is estimated by the rate-pressure product, which is:

options.A: Heart rate x systolic blood pressure
options.D: Cardiac output divided by body surface area

questions.explanation: The double product (HR x SBP) correlates with myocardial oxygen consumption.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the heart rate increases, the diastolic filling time:
questions.explanation: Tachycardia shortens diastole more than systole, reducing ventricular filling and coronary perfusion time.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE for the effect of sympathetic stimulation on the heart?

options.A: It results in vasoconstriction of cardiac (coronary) vessels
options.D: It increases rate and force of contraction

questions.explanation: Sympathetic stimulation increases rate, force and metabolism, and the coronary vessels dilate.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following can result in an increase in heart rate?

options.A: All of these: increased CO2, decreased O2 and decreased pH

questions.explanation: Hypercapnia, hypoxia and acidosis stimulate chemoreceptors and increase heart rate.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following can result in a decrease in heart rate?
questions.explanation: A rise in oxygen concentration removes the chemoreceptor drive to tachycardia.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE for hyperkalaemia?

options.A: The rate and force of contraction decrease, the PR interval and QRS widen, and T waves become tall
options.C: The rate and force of contraction increase

questions.explanation: Hyperkalaemia causes peaked T waves, wide QRS and PR prolongation, and can lead to asystole.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With an increase in peripheral resistance, the blood pressure:
questions.explanation: BP is cardiac output multiplied by total peripheral resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With a decrease in peripheral resistance, the blood pressure:
questions.explanation: Vasodilatation lowers peripheral resistance and so BP.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The amount of oxygen dissolved in 100 mL of arterial blood is about:
questions.explanation: About 0.3 mL per 100 mL is dissolved; the rest (about 20 mL) is bound to haemoglobin.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The ______ contributes to about 75% of tidal volume in quiet breathing.
questions.explanation: The diaphragm is the main inspiratory muscle.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: All of the following are accessory muscles of inspiration EXCEPT the:
questions.explanation: The diaphragm is the primary muscle of inspiration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The upward and forward movement of the sternum during ventilation, increasing the AP diameter of the thorax, is known as:
questions.explanation: Pump handle: upper ribs and sternum rise anteriorly.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The lateral flaring of the lower ribs during ventilation, increasing the transverse diameter, is known as:
questions.explanation: Bucket-handle movement affects the lower ribs.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Descent of the central tendon of the diaphragm during ventilation, increasing the vertical diameter of the thorax, is known as:
questions.explanation: The diaphragm moves downward like a piston.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal amount of air exchanged during quiet respiration (tidal volume) is about:
questions.explanation: Resting tidal volume is about 6-8 mL/kg, around 500 mL.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The amount of air a person can inhale beyond a resting inspiration is the:
questions.explanation: IRV is about 3000 mL.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The amount of air a person can exhale beyond a resting expiration is the:
questions.explanation: ERV is about 1000 mL.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Inspiratory capacity equals:
questions.explanation: IC = tidal volume plus inspiratory reserve volume.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Vital capacity equals:
questions.explanation: VC is the maximal volume exhaled after maximal inspiration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Functional residual capacity equals:
questions.explanation: FRC is the volume remaining after a quiet expiration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Total lung capacity equals:
questions.explanation: TLC is the total volume of air in the lungs after maximal inspiration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Minute ventilation equals:
questions.explanation: Minute ventilation is the total volume of air breathed per minute.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the upright position, ventilation is greater at the ______ of the lung and perfusion is greater at the ______ of the lung.
questions.explanation: Gravity favours both ventilation and perfusion at the lung bases, but perfusion more steeply.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the upright position, the ventilation-perfusion ratio is lowest (shunt-like) at the ______ of the lung.
questions.explanation: Perfusion exceeds ventilation at the base, giving a low V/Q.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the upright position, the ventilation-perfusion ratio is highest (dead-space-like) at the ______ of the lung.
questions.explanation: Ventilation exceeds perfusion at the apex.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the upright position, ventilation and perfusion are best matched (V/Q about 1) at the ______ of the lung.
questions.explanation: V/Q is close to 1 in the mid-zone.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal arterial blood pH is:
questions.explanation: Arterial pH is tightly maintained between 7.35 and 7.45.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal value of PaCO2 is:
questions.explanation: Arterial PaCO2 is 35-45 mm Hg.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal value of bicarbonate (HCO3) is:
questions.explanation: Normal arterial bicarbonate is 22-28 mEq/L.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of central venous pressure (CVP) is about:
questions.explanation: Normal CVP is about 2-8 mm Hg (0-10 in broader ranges).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal value of PaO2 is:
questions.explanation: Normal arterial oxygen tension on room air is 80-100 mm Hg.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Eccrine sweat glands mainly control:
questions.explanation: Eccrine glands cool the body by sweating.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Apocrine glands are found mainly in the:
questions.explanation: Apocrine glands become active at puberty and produce odorous secretions.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: During low-intensity, long-duration activities, which fibres are recruited?
questions.explanation: Type 1 fibres are fatigue-resistant and oxidative.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which energy system is used for activities that are highly intense but of very short duration, e.g. a 100 m sprint?
questions.explanation: The phosphagen system supplies energy for about the first 10-15 seconds.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which energy system is used for activities that are intense but short-lasting, e.g. a 400-800 m sprint?
questions.explanation: Anaerobic glycolysis supplies energy for about 30 seconds to 2 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Energy required for muscular contraction lasting up to about 15 seconds is provided by the:
questions.explanation: The creatine phosphate system provides immediate energy.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Energy required for a muscular contraction lasting up to 30-40 seconds is provided by the:
questions.explanation: Anaerobic glycolysis bridges the gap between the ATP-PC system and aerobic metabolism.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which energy system is used for low-intensity activities of long duration, e.g. a marathon?
questions.explanation: Aerobic oxidation provides sustained energy for prolonged exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of type 1 muscle fibres?
questions.explanation: Type 1 fibres are slow oxidative; fast glycolytic describes type 2b.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of type 2 muscle fibres?
questions.explanation: Slow oxidative describes type 1 fibres.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE for type 1 muscle fibres?

options.A: They are recruited during activities like sprinting
options.C: They are small with low fatiguability
options.D: Capillary density, myoglobin content and mitochondria are high

questions.explanation: Sprinting recruits type 2 (fast) fibres; type 1 fibres serve endurance activity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE for type 2 muscle fibres?

options.B: They are recruited during activities like a marathon
options.C: They are large with high fatiguability
options.D: Capillary density, myoglobin and mitochondria are low

questions.explanation: Marathon running relies on type 1 fibres.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For low-intensity, long-duration activities, which metabolism provides energy?
questions.explanation: Prolonged submaximal work depends on oxidative metabolism.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For high-intensity, short-duration activities, which metabolism provides energy?
questions.explanation: Short maximal efforts rely mainly on ATP-PC and glycolysis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
